notes:
Elicited by launching muse with --base-url pointed at a local port with nothing listening (settings.base_url, now wired into driver-interactive.sh's spawn_muse_repl). The induced failure itself is confirmed working, live, twice: both recording attempts captured terminal:"failed", reason="transport error: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:18799/responses) (after 4 provider attempts)", turn_duration_ms~2015 -- deterministic, zero API spend, resolving the prior assessment's own UNVERIFIED caveat about whether an immediate connection refusal produces the same terminal:failed shape as the two corpus samples (it does).

KNOWN_FAILING (turn_start, turn_failed, teardown): the DAEMON side of this scenario cannot be observed honestly, on 2 independent live attempts, both showing the IDENTICAL failure shape -- this is not the racy variant of the known post-birth transcript-churn bug (#1960 onboarding brief) that session-end's recording hit; here it reproduces deterministically because the turn is so fast (~2s) that the daemon never gets a chance to recover via a later re-discovery the way longer-lived sessions do. Both attempts: transcript_removed fires ~0.26-0.72s after birth (attempt 1: 06:14:30.320 birth -> 06:14:30.580 removed; attempt 2: 06:16:22.822 birth -> 06:16:23.542 removed), with NO re-discovery afterward -- yet the daemon keeps correctly tailing transcript_activity for the real session_id the entire remaining ~8s lifetime (169KB+ of real content, the 4 provider retry attempts) without EVER emitting a working or error state_transition for it. The daemon's own generic PID-liveness watch also misattributes process_exited to the session's own transient proc-<PID> presession shadow instead of the real session id, both times -- the SAME process-exit-misattribution bug (processlifecycle's watched map[int]string, last-write-wins) that hit session-end. Both of the two pre-identified daemon bugs, reproduced deterministically here, neither newly discovered -- no issue filed. daemon_capability corrected full -> bug via this observability_correction: the scenario's own defining assertion (session reaches error and stays there) is structurally unobservable through this recording pipeline for a turn this fast, not merely drifted.

session_birth and pid_bind are NOT known_failing and pass cleanly: the real session's birth (ready) and its PID binding (pid_discovered) both land correctly on its own real session_id in both attempts, independent of the later classification failure -- pid_bind is re-anchored to session_birth (not turn_start, which never matches) since it does not depend on the broken working/error classification at all. cost/tokens are asserted false: no model_completed event exists before the failure lands.
